2027-01-25.title: Monday after Kohne Sunday · Conversion of St Paul
readings: The call of Saul on the road to Damascus
He proclaims the faith he once tried to destroy
That they may all be one
2027-01-25.alt: Season of Denho. Anniversary of the erection of the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur (2010). Church Unity Octave concludes.
2027-01-25.verse: that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
theo: Our Church keeps the Conversion of Paul with the prayer of Jesus for unity. Saul, “still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord”, is thrown down by a light from heaven and hears: “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” Blind for three days, he waits in Damascus, neither eating nor drinking. Paul later tells the Galatians the whole story without hiding his past: “I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it.” Then the churches of Judea “only heard it said, ‘The one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy.’ And they glorified God because of me.”

The Gospel is from the prayer of Jesus the night before he died: “that they may all be one… so that the world may believe that you have sent me.” Division among Christians hides Christ from the world; unity reveals him. Paul, who once tore the Church apart, became the great builder of its unity. Our own Church's reunion with the See of Rome in 1930, under Mar Ivanios and his companions, sprang from that longing. Today we also give thanks for the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, erected in 2010, and pray that our Church may always be a bridge of communion.
outline: Ask: can the worst enemy of the Church become its greatest apostle?
Breathing threats, then blind and waiting.
Grace that turns a life around.

2027-01-25.prayer: Lord Jesus, you turned Saul the persecutor into Paul the apostle. Make all your disciples one, as you and the Father are one, so that the world may believe. Bless the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, and keep our Church a bridge of communion. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono we pray for the unity of the Church and receive the one Body that makes us one.

2027-01-25.question: Do I work for unity or division in my family and parish?

family.explain: Before he died, Jesus prayed for us: that we may all be one, like a family. When Christians love each other, people believe in Jesus!
family.intention: We pray for all Christians, that they may be one.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be more united as a family this week?”

illus: In a village near Adoor, Catholic, Orthodox and Marthoma families share a single cemetery road. Each year during the Unity Week their young people clean it together and pray at its end. An elderly man said: our grandfathers quarrelled over this road; our grandchildren pray on it together. That is Jesus' prayer being answered.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, make us one, as you and the Father are one. Amen.
share: Why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4). How do I treat Christ in his Church?
Now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy (Galatians 1:23). Whom have I given up on?
That they may all be one (John 17:21). What divides me from others?
interc: For the unity of all Christians.
For the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, their bishops, clergy and people.
For those hostile to the Church.
For our separated brothers and sisters in Kerala.
For our group, that we may be one in love.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that we may be one. Heal our divisions and make us witnesses of your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we keep the Conversion of St Paul. Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples, is thrown down by a light from heaven and hears: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4).

Paul does not hide his past: I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it. Then people said: the one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy (Galatians 1:13, 23). No one is beyond grace.
The Gospel is Jesus' prayer: that they may all be one, so that the world may believe that you have sent me (John 17:21). Division hides Christ; unity reveals him.
Our Church's reunion in 1930 was born of the longing for unity. Today we thank God also for the eparchies of Pathanamthitta and Puttur, and pray that we may always be a bridge of communion. Amen.
kids: Children, Saul was against Jesus, but Jesus changed him into St Paul! Jesus prays that all Christians may be one big family.
